clue.text: Cannibalistic magistrate returns God thanks

parts.note: the Doge was the chief magistrate of Venice and Genoa

indicators.note: returns means the phrase God thanks is read backwards as a whole

parts.note: taken as written
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: A man-eating official sends back his thanks to the Almighty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns the whole phrase 'God thanks' around at once, so the reversed thanks comes before the reversed deity.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog-eat-dog world is one of ruthless rivalry where people prey on their own kind, a figurative cannibalism.

clue.text: Prevent Alan forsaking star

indicators.note: forsaking means the name Alan is abandoned, its letters dropped out of the star's name

parts.note: Aldebaran is the brightest star in Taurus
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stops Alan from abandoning a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: The star is ALDEBARAN; take out A, L at the front and A, N at the back (ALAN, in order) to leave the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To debar someone is to shut them out or prohibit them, so it is a synonym of prevent.

clue.text: Take up North African drug securing a place for confinement

indicators.note: securing means holding something fast inside, so the next piece goes within
in a down clue, take up means read upwards, so the words are turned backwards

parts.note: a Moor is a North African person
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone collects a North African's narcotics, which keep a prisoner confined.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Take up' reads the Moor and the drug upwards as one run; 'securing' then has that run hold the A near its start.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardroom is a military room where prisoners are held under guard, literally a place for confinement.

clue.text: Consecration of a healing cream?

parts.note: the indefinite article a becomes an before a vowel
an ointment is a soothing salve rubbed on the skin

explanation.surface: Asking whether a holy blessing is really just a medicinal salve.
explanation.definitionFit: Anointment is the ritual application of oil to make a person or thing sacred, a form of consecration.

clue.text: Churchill ran off home with friendly swimmer

indicators.note: off means the word ran is taken away from the front of the name

parts.note: Randolph Churchill was Winston's father, and also his son
taken as written
in means at home

explanation.surface: Winston Churchill flees his house with a genial companion who swims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ran off' looks like a past-tense verb about fleeing; RAN is struck from RANDOLPH, leaving DOLPH, then IN is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolphins are sociable sea mammals famous for approaching and playing with people, hence friendly swimmers.

clue.text: Vasco's place includes also a place in Zimbabwe

indicators.note: includes means the second piece sits within the first

parts.note: Vasco da Gama: 'da Gama' marks where his family came from, so Gama is his place
too means also

explanation.surface: The navigator Vasco's home port also contains a town in Zimbabwe.
explanation.walkthrough: Vasco da Gama was the Portuguese explorer who reached India by sea; Gatooma is now called Kadoma.
explanation.definitionFit: Gatooma was a mining town in central Zimbabwe, renamed Kadoma in 1982.

clue.text: See 20
Tree kept by 21 with a spreader

indicators.note: kept by means held within, so the tree goes inside the other piece

parts.note: the answer to 21 is the first name of the writer Wilde, so 21 gives his surname
a fir is a conifer tree

explanation.surface: A conifer is looked after by an award winner, together with something that spreads.
explanation.walkthrough: A cross-reference: 21 is the prize, whose namesake is the Irish playwright, so his surname is what holds the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A wildfire spreads uncontrollably, so news that travels fast is said to spread like it.

clue.text: See 23
Last turn on French river requires ability to last

parts.note: to be last is to be at the end
a U-turn, so U stands for turn
the Rance is a river in Brittany

explanation.surface: A final turn on a river in France demands staying power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' at the start reads as a verb or adjective but gives END, while the definition reuses 'last' as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance is stamina, the capacity to keep going through hardship over a long time.

clue.text: Cheers for thug

definitions.meaning: a shout of approval, like well done
a hired ruffian or assassin, the old Italian sense of the word

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an exclamation of applause and, in older usage, a hired cutthroat.

clue.text: Odd girl inherited odd lot for show

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the following letters are put into a strange new order

explanation.surface: A peculiar girl came into a strange collection of items to put on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' signals the anagram; the second 'odd' is part of the nineteen letters of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The tale of the girl in the red hood is a staple British Christmas pantomime, a stage show.

clue.text: See 10
Republic with monarch may get friendly following

parts.note: the US is a republic
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A republic joined by a queen might earn an amiable fan base.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic prompt: the word can be followed by 'friendly' to make user-friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Software made easy for people who operate it is called user-friendly, so this word can take friendly after it.

clue.text: Show flag with article in old city gossip

parts.note: a jack is a ship's flag, as in Union Jack
and means together with

indicators.note: in means the article is placed inside the city's name

parts.note: Thebes was an ancient city in Egypt and in Greece
an is the indefinite article
talk means gossip

explanation.surface: A banner and a grammatical article end up as chatter in an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the article inside the ancient city, so the city's name splits across the third and fourth words of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The story of the boy who climbs a giant plant is a classic Christmas pantomime show.

clue.text: Authority for degree captured by good scholar

indicators.note: captured by means held inside, so these pieces sit within the other

parts.note: bon is French for good
OK is approval or authorisation
an MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: Approval for a qualification is seized by a fine scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good scholar' looks like the definition with an adjective; 'good' is the French word wrapped around the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookman is a learned person devoted to books, a literary scholar.

clue.text: See 13
Show a boy to row

parts.note: taken as written
a lad is a boy
a din is a noisy row

explanation.surface: Instructions to show a boy how to handle the oars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' rhymes with 'go' in the surface but is the noun meaning a racket.
explanation.definitionFit: The story of the boy with the magic lamp is a well-known Christmas pantomime show.

clue.text: Blows up 10 with dismay, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps means the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: the numeral 10 read as the word ten
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cross-reference to 10 and alarm explodes.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a reference to the answer at 10 but is just the number TEN, mixed with DISMAY.
explanation.definitionFit: To dynamite something is to blast it with explosives, so dynamites means blows up.

clue.text: Annual expression of regret about chap losing monarch

indicators.note: losing means the monarch's letter is dropped from what is built
about means surrounding, so the regret goes around the chap

parts.note: alack is an old cry of sorrow
a man is a chap
K stands for king

explanation.surface: A yearly display of sorrow over a man who has lost his king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the cry of regret around the chap, which makes an old spelling of the answer; 'losing' then removes the king's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is a yearbook, and 'annual' as a noun means a book published once a year.

clue.text: Short show that's burnt out

definitions.meaning: a pet-name abbreviation of the pantomime heroine with the glass slipper
the residue of coal or wood after burning

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an affectionate short form of a pantomime heroine's name and the burnt remains of a fire.

clue.text: Obliquely request an established body

parts.note: to ask is to request
taken as written
CE is the Church of England, the established church

explanation.surface: Ask sideways for a recognised institution.
explanation.walkthrough: The Church of England is the 'established' church, meaning it is the official state church in England.
explanation.definitionFit: To look askance is to glance sideways, obliquely, often with suspicion.

clue.text: A changed sect in charge of yogi

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: changed means the letters of sect are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A transformed religious group is led by a yogi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges SECT into SCET; 'yogi' looks like a person being put in charge but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A yogi practises self-denial and austere discipline, so is an example of an ascetic.

clue.text: Show whose twin is shown

parts.note: a pantomime whose heroine, in a Grimm tale, has a sister named Rose-Red, the other colour also seen in the show at 10

explanation.walkthrough: A cryptic definition: the pantomime heroine has a twin sister in Grimm, and that sister's colour also appears in the show at 10, which is shown in this grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy tale of the princess and the seven dwarfs is a favourite Christmas pantomime.

clue.text: Prize for 4x4?

parts.note: OS means outsize, and a four-by-four is an outsize vehicle
a four-by-four is a type of car

explanation.surface: An award for a big off-road vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: A 4x4 is a large four-wheel-drive vehicle, read here as an OS (outsize) CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oscar is the Academy Award statuette given for achievement in film.

clue.text: Not paying a foreign female jester that keeps on

parts.note: une is the French feminine word for a

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so on goes within the jester

parts.note: a comic is a jester
taken as written

explanation.surface: An overseas woman doing jokes who won't stop does not earn money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' puts ON inside the jester just after his first letter, making CONOMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An uneconomic venture fails to make a profit, so it does not pay.

clue.text: Mount for rebel horseman is lacking energy

parts.note: Jack Cade led a rebellion in Kent in 1450

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so energy's letter is taken away

parts.note: a rider is a horseman
E is the physics symbol for energy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mount for an insurgent rider who has run out of steam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' drops the energy letter from the horseman and 'is' together, and the result follows the rebel's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cader Idris is a mountain in Snowdonia, Wales, and mount means a mountain.

clue.text: See 6
Put note in crate to be translated by planner

indicators.note: in means the note is put inside the crate
translated means changed into another form, so the combined letters are rearranged

parts.note: a chit is a short note

explanation.surface: Someone puts a memo in a box to be converted by a designer.
explanation.walkthrough: CHIT goes into CRATE and the whole is rearranged; 'Put' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: An architect plans and designs buildings, so is a planner.

clue.text: Brought to bear?

parts.note: taken as written
Ted, short for teddy, is a toy bear

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as the idiom 'brought to bear', but it splits after the first word, with a teddy giving the bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Toted means carried, so it is a synonym for brought.

clue.text: Neighbours' girl has complete change of heart in the mass

indicators.note: the central letter of the girl's name is swapped for a different one

parts.note: Kylie Minogue played Charlene in the Australian soap Neighbours

explanation.surface: An actress from a soap undergoes a total turnaround of feeling during church service.
explanation.walkthrough: Neighbours is an Australian TV soap opera hugely popular in Britain; the heart of KYLIE, L, becomes R.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kyrie eleison is the opening sung prayer of the Mass, so it occurs in the mass.

clue.text: Next one to win gets gold

parts.note: a win is a success
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: To be the next winner one needs gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A successor is the next one to follow in a role or line.
